title: Tenant-adaptive ingest parser and backpressure policy for structured logs
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Our current log ingestion pipeline accepts JSON blobs from many tenants but struggles when tenants send high-cardinality labels, partially structured payloads, or sudden burst traffic. Downstream Loki clusters see label explosion, parsing errors, and spikes that increase cost and cause elevated ingest latency.

Goal: Implement a tenant-adaptive ingest parser and coordinated backpressure policy at the edge (Vector/Fluentd layer) that: 1) enforces per-tenant schema rules with graceful schema evolution; 2) applies adaptive sampling and KV-label pruning for high-cardinality tenants; 3) surfaces parse failures and suppression metrics to Grafana; and 4) triggers coordinated backpressure/fallback routing to a low-fidelity writepath when upstream is overloaded.

Non-goals: Full rework of Loki retention or alerting. We won't replace storage tier decisions in this ticket; focus is ingest-time transformations and routing decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Edge parser validates JSON payloads against tenant-specific schema (fallback to default schema) and emits structured fields for downstream indexing
High-cardinality label pruning policy can be configured per-tenant and automatically applied when distinct_label_count > threshold
Adaptive sampling reduces tokenized event rate to Loki by configurable percentage for bursty tenants and falls back when burst subsides
Backpressure path routes to low-fidelity bucket (compressed, minimal labels) and returns 429/202 semantics to SDKs depending on tenant SLAs
Unit and integration tests exercising schema evolution, label pruning, and backpressure; performance test shows <15ms median additional latency at edge under normal load
Grafana dashboard panel added showing parse_error_rate, pruned_label_rate, sampled_event_rate, backpressure_events by tenant
notes:
Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Tenant+Adaptive+Ingest+Parser
Initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/337
Load test artifact: s3://redwood-performance/ingest/2025-02-25/tenant-adapt-proto.tar.gz
implementation_plan: Week 1: Design schema rules DSL and vertex for tenant configs; add config store entries and TTL semantics
Week 2: Implement Vector transform for schema validation + label pruning; add adaptive-sampler subcomponent
Week 3: Implement backpressure routing with two writepaths (full-fidelity -> Loki ; low-fidelity -> archival S3 or compressed Loki stream)
Week 4: Integrate metrics (parse_errors, pruned_labels, sampling_rate, backpressure_count) and instrument Grafana panels; run perf tests
Rollout: Canary 5 tenants -> 25 tenants -> all tenants with automatic rollback on error budget breaches
testing_plan: Unit tests for parser DSL, schema fallback rules, and pruning logic (jest/go tests)
Integration tests with local Loki stack and Vector in CI (docker-compose) exercising label explosion scenarios
Synthetic load tests recreating burst patterns from customer telemetry (scripts in performance repo)
Chaos test: force Loki ingestion throttling and validate edge backpressure activates and SDK responses match SLA mappings
monitoring_and_alerting: Grafana dashboard: 'Ingest — Tenant Adaptive' (panel ids in design doc)
Alerts: Alert if parse_error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m or backpressure_events > 1% of tenant traffic
SLO ties: Backpressure activation counts should not exceed configured budget per tenant; incidents create automatic pager for infra on P0 tenants
rollout_notes: Canary plan requires whitelist of 5 low-risk tenants (contact list stored in Confluence doc)
Feature flag inbound: OBS.tenant_adaptive_ingest (default off). Use rollout strategy tied to tenant config override
Rollback strategy: Flip flag -> drain low-fidelity stream -> rehydrate suspected missing events from buffer when safe
